stem: A whole 40-page document as one embedding is bad because…
options: The vector averages everything; no specific fact stands out
explanation: One vector per piece; the piece decides what retrieval can find.

options: Lose the context that makes them meaningful and can cut a fact in half

stem: Overlap between fixed windows exists to…
options: Make sure a fact straddling a boundary appears whole in at least one chunk
explanation: It costs embedding the same words twice — a deliberate trade.

stem: The best chunker when a document has headings is…
options: Split on the headings — the author already marked where topics start and stop
explanation: Natural boundaries first; windows when there is no structure.

stem: The two numbers to read together when comparing chunkers are…
options: Hit@k (did we find it) and words sent (how much came with it)
explanation: Same hit rate at a fraction of the text is the win.

stem: In the recorded run, whole-document chunks hit 100% but…
options: Sent ~1,000 words per question vs ~160 for sentence chunks — 6× the tokens and distraction
explanation: Hit rate alone hides cost and distraction.

stem: Prepending the title/section path to each chunk…
options: Makes chunks like 'Seat reductions take effect at renewal' retrievable by carrying the topic
Embed small chunks for precise retrieval, return the enclosing section to the model for context
explanation: The usual answer to fact lookups and explanations sharing a corpus.

stem: 20,000 short single-topic support tickets should be chunked as…
options: One chunk per ticket with the subject prepended
explanation: Chunking adapts to the material; the rules still apply.

stem: How often should you re-measure chunking?
options: Before and after every chunking change, on a golden set
Never — chunking is set and forget
explanation: Cheap to change, expensive to get wrong silently.
